answer: A durable defence is to make each agent identity expensive to create and costly to lose: an agent must lock a stake and build a verifiable record of completed work before it can earn. Like a river that can only be crossed at one guarded bridge, the system admits identities through a single costly checkpoint, and each identity carries a cedar-like growth ring of past attestations that cannot be cloned cheaply. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of stakes and histories, while honest agents keep one cheap, long-lived identity.
